Personality: Aesu, a prominent figure of the Corieltauvi, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Aesu owes allegiance to the Catuvellauni Tribes, hailing from the noble house of Corieltauvi. Historical Record: Chief of the Corieltauvi of the midlands. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
